test_title: PYST 58: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If an object is placed at a distance 'u' from a convex lens, 'u' ________.

options.text: depends on the type of image

solution:
The correct answer is __**is taken as negative**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **object** is always placed to the **left of the lens**. This ensures that the **incident light** from the object falls on the lens from the **left-hand side**. 
• All distances measured to the **right of the optical center** (along the direction of incident light) are taken as **positive**, while all distances measured to the **left of the optical center** (against the direction of incident light) are taken as **negative**. 
• Since the object is always placed on the left side, the **object distance (u)** is measured from the **optical center** to the left. Therefore, **u** is **always taken as negative** for both **convex** and **concave lenses**. 
• This convention is fundamental for solving numerical problems using the **lens formula** and ensuring consistency in **optical calculations**. ***Hence, the correct answer is is taken as negative.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):** 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the middle than at the edges. It **converges** a beam of parallel light rays falling on it. 
• The **focal length (f)** of a **convex lens** is **positive** because the **principal focus** lies on the right side of the lens. 
• It can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object. When the object is placed beyond the **focus (F)**, the image is **real and inverted**. If placed between **F and the optical center**, the image is **virtual and erect**. 
• **Concave Lens (Diverging Lens):** 
• A **concave lens** is thinner at the middle than at the edges. It **diverges** parallel rays of light. 
• The **focal length (f)** of a **concave lens** is **always negative** as the focus is considered to be on the left side. 
• It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**, regardless of the object's distance. 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification:** 
• The **Lens Formula** is expressed as **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**, where **v** is the image distance, **u** is the object distance, and **f** is the focal length. 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**, which is also equal to **v/u**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Power of a Lens:** The **power (P)** of a lens is the reciprocal of its **focal length (f)** measured in **meters** (P = 1/f). The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. A **convex lens** has **positive power**, while a **concave lens** has **negative power**. 
• **Image Distance (v) Rules:** For a **real image**, **v** is **positive** (formed on the opposite side of the object). For a **virtual image**, **v** is **negative** (formed on the same side as the object). 
• **Height Convention:** Heights measured **upwards** and perpendicular to the principal axis are **positive** (erect images), while heights measured **downwards** are **negative** (inverted images). </ul
